land.text: 'As a result of the alliance with the Spaniards, Tlaxcala had hidalgo privileged status within New Spain'

successors.note: Allied with Cortes on 23 September 1519 and 'allowed to survive and preserve its pre-Columbian culture'; the four lordships (Ocotelolco, Quiahuiztlan, Tepeticpac, Tizatlan) were fixed by the Spanish corregidor in 1545.

capitals.name: Tlaxcala (Tepeticpac Texcallan)
capitals.note: The page names no pre-Columbian capital: 'a third group arrived in the modern valley of Tlaxcala, where they established the city of Tepeticpac Texcallan'; Ocotelulco, Tizatlan and Quiahuiztlan were four seats of a confederacy. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Tlaxcala.

correction.text: The Tlaxcala valley, 'completely surrounded by Aztec lands': the modern state of Tlaxcala stands for the confederacy's territory

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks Tlaxcala). The page gives no area and no boundary: 'Tlaxcala was completely surrounded by Aztec lands, leading to intermittent armed conflict'. The modern state (about 4,000 km2) is my reading; Cliopatria's Aztec shape contains the whole of it from 1482, which the Aztec Triple Alliance dossier cuts out. Infobox span 1348-1520.

region.text: the Tlaxcala valley: Tepeticpac, Ocotelolco, Tizatlan, Quiahuiztlan

ledger.note: 1348: the Tlaxcalans settle their valley and found Tepeticpac Texcallan. The infobox span is 1348-1520 and lists '1348' beside the 'Tlaxcaltec migration to Central Mexico'; the body gives no year for the founding of Tepeticpac, Ocotelolco, Tizatlan or Quiahuiztlan, so the date is the infobox's (confidence 1).

1521: Tlaxcala, Cortes's ally since 23 September 1519, passes into New Spain with privileges. The Tlaxcala page's infobox ends in 1520 and does not describe a dissolution; 1521 is the fall of Tenochtitlan (13 August 1521) and the year of Cliopatria's Spanish Empire row (page silent, confidence 1).

wars.name: Flower wars
wars.outcome: Intermittent ritual wars between the Triple Alliance and the cities of the Tlaxcala-Puebla valley; Tlaxcala was never conquered. Infobox 'Cholula and Atlixco incorporated into the Aztec Empire'.
wars.note: Infobox '1454 - 1519 (65 Years)'. Ixtlilxochitl reports they began as a response to the famine of 1450-1454. The Tlaxcala page has the Aztec trade embargo (no year) and Motecuhzoma I's flower-war policy. They take no ground, so no contest is drawn.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire (Tlaxcalan alliance)
wars.outcome: Tlaxcala fought the Spaniards in three battles on 2-5 September 1519 and allied with Cortes on 23 September 1519; its warriors took part in the siege of Tenochtitlan (10 May to 13 August 1521).
wars.note: The Tlaxcala page has Xicohtencatl the Younger 'condemned by the Tlaxcalan ruling council and hanged by Cortes' in April 1521.

certainty.note: No boundary is described; the enclave is the modern state by my reading.

sources.title: Tlaxcala (Nahua state)
sources.note: The request for Republic_of_Tlaxcala returned the article 'Confederacy of Tlaxcala' (infobox span 1348-1520): four lordships, surrounded by Aztec lands, embargo, privileges.

sources.title: Flower war
sources.note: Infobox 1454-1519; 1450-1454 drought origin; enemies Tlaxcala, Huejotzingo and Cholula.

sources.title: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire
sources.note: Tlaxcalan battles 2-5 September 1519 and alliance 23 September 1519; siege 10 May to 13 August 1521.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks Tlaxcala). Three pages (budget 2-5). (1) The article opened under Republic_of_Tlaxcala is titled 'Tlaxcala (Nahua state)' / 'Confederacy of Tlaxcala'; wikidata is unknown (null). (2) START 1348 is the infobox's migration/span year, not a body-text founding date (confidence 1). (3) END: the infobox ends 1520; 1521 is chosen to coincide with the Aztec fall and Cliopatria's Spanish row; Tlaxcala was not conquered but an ally with privileges, so a rendering might prefer a vassal tint of the Spanish Empire from 1519. (4) The territory is the modern Tlaxcala state, an assumption; the pages say only 'completely surrounded by Aztec lands'. (5) Huejotzingo, Cholula (dossier cholula exists, by another group) and Atlixco are the other Puebla-Tlaxcala valley cities; Cholula 'became an Aztec tributary' in 1517 (Spanish conquest page). Huejotzingo has no dossier.
